records.title: First regular meetup
records.summary: The team shared expectations, goals, strengths, and weaknesses. Members discussed project quality and possible voice services. The project topic remains open.
agenda: Introductions and questions prepared by the leader
Discussion of feasibility, user needs, and expected effects
Vehicle agent: voice navigation, warning light explanations, and service bookings
Personal tutor with voice and vision
Voice notes during manual work, with organized work records
Childcare assistant that learns from baby cries
Voice control for apps with visual menus
Exercise assistant: running coaching, gym support, and hiking guidance and alerts
Voice home assistant for people who live alone, including older adults
Shopping agent: ingredient planning, quantities, discounts, and store routes
Real-time assistance for people with visual impairments, using voice and vision
decisions: Build a useful service with a complete user scenario and quality suitable for a portfolio. An MVP alone is not the final goal.
Shared GitHub and OpenAI Organization account information for collaboration.
Do not use the program facilitator assistant.

Use approximately KRW 400,000 of the leader facilitator allowance for voice API costs. Members expressed willingness to contribute some personal funds if needed. Costs remain uncertain, and excessive personal costs could be difficult. Ask for news of support programs.
next_steps: Set criteria to compare ideas and select the project topic.

records.title: Second regular meetup: project selection
records.summary: The team selected MIND DETOXING. An overtime discussion explored voice-based thought dumping, everyday reflection, and personal patterns. Product scope, roles, and milestones remain open.
agenda: Review project proposals and vote on the team project.
Explore a lighter reflection service after the meetup.
decisions: MIND DETOXING is the selected team project.
next_steps: Define users, scope, roles, and milestones in a separate discussion.

sections.title: Other project ideas
paragraphs: The following pros and cons are retrospective assessments added to this report. They are not confirmed statements from the meeting or reasons for individual votes.

tables.label: Project idea comparison
rows: Docent: multilingual exhibition guide
A clear setting for follow-up questions and multilingual conversation.
Official exhibition materials can ground answers.
A pilot can start with one exhibit and one tablet.
Realistic testing needs an exhibition partner.
Noise and reluctance to speak in public may limit use.
Content updates and answer checks require ongoing work.
VoiceQuest: multiplayer voice mystery game
Team members can test the game together.
The game tests turn-taking, interruptions, and shared context.
One short mystery gives the prototype a clear scope.
Enjoyment depends heavily on story quality.
Simultaneous speakers make interaction difficult.
Spoilers or inconsistent clues can break the game.
VoiceFit: voice-controlled workout assistant
Hands-free control addresses a concrete inconvenience.
Timers, pauses, and corrections give measurable tasks.
User-defined routines reduce the need for specialist content.
Existing timers may already meet user needs.
Breathing and background noise can reduce recognition quality.
Incorrect timing or commands can disrupt exercise.
Reservation assistant: AI phone bookings
The service completes a concrete task.
It can reach businesses without online booking.
It tests conversation, negotiation, and delegated actions.
Phone integration adds cost and complexity.
Staff may decline or struggle with AI calls.
Ambiguous answers can cause incorrect booking confirmations.
Voice body double: help with task completion
The service addresses difficulty starting and finishing tasks.
It tests proactive check-ins and persistent task state.
Completion and repeat use give concrete evaluation measures.
Check-ins may feel intrusive or like nagging.
Scheduling and reconnection add complexity.
Use may decline after the initial novelty fades.
FamilySync: shared family scheduling
The service addresses recurring coordination needs.
It tests multi-user context and consent.
A three-person scenario gives a focused prototype.
Adoption needs participation from several family members.
Speaker identification and calendar access add complexity.
Permission or schedule errors can undermine trust.

sections.title: Overtime discussion: everyday reflection
paragraphs: After the meetup, a few members explored a lighter role than specialized mental healthcare. These ideas did not finalize the product scope.

after.title: Service role: everyday reflection
paragraphs: The team explored help with expressing and organizing everyday thoughts, with a lighter role than specialized mental healthcare.

after.title: Speak, organize, gain distance, notice patterns
items: A hands-free brain dump could let users speak freely instead of typing, then review an organized account of their day.
Distance from their thoughts may help users view situations more objectively and notice recurring triggers or patterns. A personal checklist was suggested.

after.title: Conditions for use and trust
items: Users need private time and a space where they can speak comfortably. Some users value writing by hand, so the team must examine when speech is useful.
People may share worries with a trusted listener who helps them notice assumptions, biases, mistaken judgments, or leaps in reasoning. A diary or spoken account can still be selective or incomplete.
